intervals.label: dark matter phase of IGEX at Canfranc (one enriched 76Ge detector)
intervals.note: Start: bounded by the first IGEX-DM paper (February 2000), which says 'A recent upgrade has made it possible to use them in a search for WIMPs'; the start of the dark matter phase is not dated. End: bounded by the November 2002 status talk that has the experiment 'currently operating'.
intervals.quote: are currently operating in the Canfranc Underground Laboratory with an overburden of 2450 m.w.e. A recent upgrade has made it possible to use them in a search for WIMPs.

intervals.label: completed (no end date published)
intervals.note: Year of the latest source read (November 2002); no source states when the dark matter phase ended. Its proposed extension, GEDEON, is not recorded (no design report or approval).
intervals.quote: The IGEX dark matter experiment is currently operating one germanium detector with this purpose in the Canfranc Underground Laboratory.

summary.plain: IGEX-DM was the dark matter search of the International Germanium Experiment. One 2-kilogram germanium crystal, made for a rare-decay study, was used deep under the Pyrenees at Canfranc to look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium, and set limits on their interaction.
summary.technical: The low-energy data acquisition of an IGEX 76Ge (enriched to 86%) double-beta detector (2.2 kg, ~2.0 kg active; called RG-2 in a 2000 proceedings) with ~4 keV threshold, in IGEX's 2.5 t archaeological-lead shield with muon veto and neutron moderator, in the Canfranc laboratory (2450 m.w.e.). Spin-independent WIMP-nucleon exclusion plots from 30 days (2000) and 40 days (2002) of raw data; the 2002 contour enters the DAMA region.

technology.quote: One of the IGEX detectors of 2.2
technology.value: A 2.2 kg p-type high-purity germanium detector, enriched to 86% in 76Ge, read out at low energy in a lead, polyethylene and muon-veto shield
